speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where your abdominal pain is located and how it feels? Also, when did the pain first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack and the sudden onset of pain with bloody stools, have you noticed any fever, chills, or significant dizziness? Do you have a history of atrial fibrillation or prior episodes of similar abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack, do you have a history of atrial fibrillation or any other irregular heart rhythms? Additionally, is the pain currently constant, or does it come and go in waves?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. History of acute myocardial infarction. Social history: Smokes 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your heavy smoking history and the nature of your pain, have you noticed any tenderness when I press on your abdomen, or does the area feel unusually soft compared to the severity of the pain? Also, is your blood pressure currently stable or lower than usual?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, vomiting. Reports bloody loose bowel movements.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the abdomen and pelvis. Given your history of smoking, recent heart attack, and bloody stools with severe pain, I need to urgently check for a blockage in your mesenteric arteries.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Angiography Abdomen: Evidence suggestive of reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries. Abdominal Examination: Bruit heard over the epigastric area; Mild periumbilical tenderness. Vital Signs: Heart Rate 95 bpm, Blood Pressure 95/65 mm Hg, Temperature 36.9°C (98.4°F).

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT results and your vital signs strongly indicate Acute Mesenteric Ischemia, likely caused by an embolus from your recent heart attack or severe atherosclerosis given your smoking history. With reduced blood flow to your intestines and signs of low perfusion, this is a surgical emergency requiring immediate intervention. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia
